items.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: John Guerin is the drummer, the drummer I mentioned earlier, and Chuck Domenico.

ctx.x: That was some nice stuff there.

Roger had not been in L.A. very long. He had come out from New York when he did that and he had only been in L.A. a year or two when I first met him out here. I’d been aware of him from an early recording he’d made in New York, but yeah, that’s an interesting, and John Guerin is the drummer, the drummer I mentioned earlier, and Chuck Domenico. But again, for someone, I’m sixty years old, and particularly for people my age, both the players and the audience, usually I find in talking with them they have become…

happen. I feel very strongly that that’s not — I don’t want that to be the way one ages. I think it’s much more important — I’m really fascinated with what young people are thinking and how they hear it and how they see it. And I think world music, for lack of a better category, is here definitely bigger than ever. I think Cuban music obviously is having a tremendous effect on what goes on here. I think in the next few years we’re going to see more and more of that influence. And so much of what goes on in the…
